If sentiment is negative in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.5% in early horizon (1–7 days) to align with downward momentum.  
If sentiment is positive and price is trending up, increase forecast by 1.0–2.0% in mid horizon (8–15 days) to capture bullish momentum.  
If sentiment is mixed or neutral and price is volatile, apply a 0.5–1.5% downward adjustment in late horizon (16–30 days) to dampen overconfidence.  
When sentiment shifts from positive to negative within 5 days, reduce forecast slope by 20–30% in early horizon to reflect sentiment reversal.  
If sentiment is consistently positive over 10+ days, increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day in mid horizon to reflect sustained bullish bias.  
If sentiment is negative and forecast is above 70, apply a 2.0–3.0% downward correction in late horizon to prevent overextension.
